column1: # THE WAYS BETWEEN PLACES. Reference, and it used to be a dict inside a tool.
# `ROADS` lived hard-coded in tools/overland.py, which is data in code -- the one
# thing CLAUDE.md is most insistent about. It is a file now.
# *** `kind` IS MECHANICAL, NOT DECORATIVE. *** rules/overland.md, DMG p.58:
# "Normal terrain ... with respect to vehicular movement it assumes ROADWAYS
# through such terrain", and "Rugged ... assumes either roadways through such
# terrain OR TRACKS/PATHS through normal terrain". So:
#   road    normal for a vehicle   cart 25 mi/day, mount 40
#   track   RUGGED for a vehicle   cart 15 mi/day, mount 20. A cart CAN take it
#   path    not cart-passable at all -- feet and hooves only
# That is why a day off the road to Lyde is eighteen miles and not twenty-five.
# `stops` is a comma list of place ids IN ORDER. A junction is a place: the
# turnings below exist so that "how do you get to Lyde" has an answer that is

South-west. The road the party first came in by, before expedition 1

column2: the east road out of Ludbury
column5: THREE DAYS EAST. The party has never been on it and knows only that it exists

DM CALL 2026-09-12: Lyde is reached by a TURNING off the north road about two days south of Wethersby, then eighteen miles west. NOT via Draycot and NOT via Marchford. Eighteen miles of track is "a day off the road each way" for a rider -- which is the attested phrase, and is why Wat rode rather than carted
Four miles east off the north road. The record's own words: "four acres of flax FOUR MILES EAST OF THE ROAD"

DM CALL 2026-09-12: *** THERE IS NO DIRECT WAY TO EDE'S FROM THE MAIN ROAD. *** Her gate is reached THROUGH FENN'S YARD, eight miles of field track, which is why the party has gone that way both times and why Halm's cart could fetch her load at all. It makes Fenn's the gateway to her, which is worth knowing before anybody plans around her

column2: the south road out of Draycot
column5: *** INFERRED FROM THE RECORD, NOT INVENTED. *** district.md: "Sir Aymer's clip has gone [to Ludbury] these two summers", and Wethersby was never told where the staple went because "his clip goes to Ludbury EITHER WAY". If it went through Wethersby the town would have watched it go, every summer, and the whole mystery would never have existed. So it does not: Draycot has its own way south. About a hundred miles, four days by cart. *** KNOWN TO THE PARTY AS OF DAY 146 -- Darrow named it plainly when asked what roads leave Ludbury (146:3, knowledge.tsv). Not a secret, just never asked ***
The Draycot road does not STOP at Draycot -- it carries on south-west, out of the hundred, and it is the road the party walked in by before expedition 1. They know it exists because they came up it

*** THE ONLY MADE WAY ON THE CRAG AND IT WAS NOT THERE BEFORE DAY 20. *** Coll's crew graded it: half an hour off the north road, cart-passable to the basecamp flat and NO FURTHER. Written into the licence by Master Wace as works erected by the licensee, so it is lawful as well as useful

*** A CART NEVER REACHES THE DOOR. *** Half an hour of UNMADE OUTCROP above the basecamp -- feet and hooves only. The DM twice described the graded trail as reaching the cave door; it does not, it reaches halfway, and Halm's objection to the rope plan collapsed with that correction

THE WAY TO THE GNOME RENDEZVOUS (L053), AND THE PARTY HAS NEVER SET FOOT ON IT. Round the crag's north shoulder from the basecamp flat to the mouth of the dry watercourse. NOT A MADE WAY -- there is no trail, only the line a cart could be walked if the ground allows, and whether it allows is a thing to be found out on the ground and not asserted from a map

*** THE LAST MILE OF THE NORTH ROAD, AND IT IS NOT REALLY ROAD. *** From the crag turning it runs on as a cart-width of beaten dirt for about a mile and then simply stops (d6=2, day 98). Kept as a separate way from north_road ON PURPOSE: the spine is a made road at 25 miles a day for a cart and THIS IS NOT, so calling it the same thing would let a cart be routed up it at road speed

*** THE WAY THE GNOMES' CART CAN STAND AT THAT MOUTH. *** Open rough ground, no trail, ~3.7 miles between the road's end and the mouth of the dry watercourse. Ridden day 98 by Dave, Yrtone and Hask coming the other way. d6=4: IT RIDES, CAREFULLY, AND IT IS NOT PLAINLY BETTER THAN THE SCREE -- which is the answer the ride was sent to get. Nearly twice as far as the 2 miles round the north foot from the basecamp, and better going per mile. The party may take either on the 101st and neither is obviously right
